name: btn
description: The one button. Every affirmative, neutral, destructive and marketing action on every surface is this unit with a different variant — six variants and four sizes, which is what the estate actually contains once the hand-written ones are counted.

base.transition: background var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out), transform var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out)

primary.$description: the one main affirmative action on a surface.

secondary.$description: neutral. An outline and dark text, never a coloured fill — a secondary action that carries a fill competes with the primary beside it.

danger.$description: destructive. The same variant on the trigger AND on its confirm dialog — red in one place and blue in the other is the bug this rule exists to stop.

ghost.$description: no chrome at all, for a tertiary action inside dense UI.

accent.$description: the marketing call to action — sunflower, the one place the brand shouts. Distinct from `primary` on purpose: primary is the main affirmative action on a form, accent is the thing the page is FOR. Ink is accent-foreground (8.77:1), never the page greys.

unavailable.$description: not offered yet. NOT `disabled`: disabled means you may not, and this means there is nothing here to press. A muted fill rather than a dimmed primary, because dimming a primary reads as a control that failed rather than one that has not arrived.

lg.$description: a section CTA. 2.75rem clears the 44px touch target with room to spare.

xl.$description: the one submit a page is built around — the name check.

hover.$description: A lift rather than a fade. Fading a button on hover says "less", which is the opposite of what a hover means; 1px of travel and a shadow say "this is reachable".

disabled.$description: Flat and quiet, not a dimmed slab. Reducing a filled button to 55% opacity over a cream page produces a muddy grey that reads as a control that failed rather than one that is not available yet — so the fill is dropped instead of faded.

loading.$description: Full strength, cursor progress. Reusing the disabled treatment for an in-flight action reads as "you cannot do this" rather than "this is happening".

reducedMotion.$description: The press feedback goes; the control still responds. Never `animation:none` as a blanket — a button has no entrance animation to lose, but the rule is written per unit because for others it would remove the very thing that reveals the content.

a11y.keyboard: Enter and Space activate. Tab reaches it. Disabled removes it from the tab order.
a11y.notes: `loading` deliberately keeps full opacity and swaps the cursor: an action in flight must not read as unavailable. aria-busy carries the announcement.
